title: Disney to Pay $210M for Character.AI Staff in Bankruptcy Deal
summary:
A new agreement to preserve the careers of several dozen engineers and staff members is pending approval from a judge overseeing the insolvency of a chatbot developer. Disney will pay roughly $180 million over three years to hire more than 60 Character.AI employees, adding $30 million in retention bonuses to the compensation package. This recruitment deal is separate from a $20 million opening bid Disney made to acquire intellectual property and specific legal claims from the startup.

Character Technologies filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware after failing to manage costly lawsuits involving teen suicide and self-harm. Court documents show the company was losing $9 million a month, spending $14 million monthly on compute costs against $1 million in revenue. The collapse follows a 2024 licensing deal with Google worth $2.7 billion that rehired the founders while leaving the company's legal liabilities behind. A court-supervised auction for the remaining assets is slated to close by December.

selectedTweets.text:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: Character .ai filed for bankruptcy, going from a $2.7 billion Google deal to a $20 million Disney sale.

• Disney is paying $20M for some assets and a perpetual license to its tech, and the platform shuts down if no buyer keeps it running
• Founders Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas left Google in 2021 after it refused to release Meena, the chatbot they built there
• In 2024, Google paid $2.7B to license its tech and rehire them. Shazeer helped turn Gemini around, then left for OpenAI in under 2 years
• It peaked at 20M monthly users, then faced lawsuits over teen safety, including a settled case over a 14-year-old's suicide
• It lost its top talent twice, to Google and then to Disney along with its CEO last month, banned under-18 users and cut open-ended chat
• The rest of AI has growing users and few legal headwinds, so this isn't a sign of a bust, but it previews what heavy regulation could do

selectedTweets.text:
hot AI startup character ai just filed for bankruptcy! https://t.co/TqtIm0p8LV

i gathered insights from the actual bankruptcy filing itself https://t.co/OnZvWnwe5W and this is an interesting one to break down

1. they have adoption and engagement

12M MAU, with average 2 hours of daily time spent per user! 

that’s.. quite a lot. many startup products would dream to reach this level of usage, but it didn’t work

2. they have real network effect

they have user generated characters and many users like to engage with characters made by others. so the more users they have, the richer this ecosystem becomes - textbook network effect

some people seem to think network effect is gold. nope! didn’t work

3. they have proprietary data and custom trained models

many people say software is dead and only data is moat. this gives a sobering look - private data didn’t help either

4. so what’s wrong?

they burn over $7M of compute and only get $5M of revenue per month

that’s the whole problem

people would engage for free or when subsidized, but they are not willing to pay enough $ for the value they are getting

now… the real dark side of this 

if you take a few steps back and look at all LLM usage, especially all the people on social media using tokens to make the same 3d demos every day - 

how many people are actually creating more economical value than the tokens they burnt? if there’s no subsidization and everyone has to pay at API price, how much of the current usage can actually be justified with positive ROI and sustain? 

we have limited runway to make AI work. and if we can’t, what happened to character ai may just be a preview for the entire AI industry
